deals.travelWindow: Sep 5 – Nov 14, cheapest is the Nov 7 departure
deals.whyRanked: $93 RT on Allegiant for the Nov 7 departure — a new low and still the cheapest fare of the five — with the Smokies' Greenbrier entrance 45 minutes away.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown's compact grid is easy to explore solo on foot, and the park's Greenbrier and Cosby entrances offer quiet trails away from the Cades Cove crowds.

highlights: Ijams Nature Center's quarry swimming hole and trails
Concord Park on Fort Loudoun Lake
Knoxville Museum of Art overlooking World's Fair Park
Great Smoky Mountains NP's Greenbrier entrance
itinerary: Day 1 — Ijams Nature Center trails and quarry overlook, dinner in the Old City.
Day 2 — Knoxville Museum of Art and World's Fair Park in the morning, South Waterfront Riverwalk at sunset.
Day 3 — Rent a car for Greenbrier: Ramsey Cascades or the Porters Creek trailhead before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown, Ijams, and the South Waterfront are walkable or a short bike ride; a rental car is required to reach the national park.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near Gay Street or the South Waterfront — walkable, close to the Riverwalk and Old City nightlife.

deals.whyRanked: $131 RT nonstop on American for Saturday departures through December — back at the same low it hit a week ago, still a rare dip under $180 on this route.
deals.soloWhy: Uptown and Deep Ellum are walkable, transit-friendly pockets, though the city overall is spread out enough that a car or rideshare budget helps.

highlights: Dallas Museum of Art (free general admission)
Deep Ellum street art and live music
itinerary: Day 1 — Dallas Museum of Art, Klyde Warren Park for lunch, Reunion Tower at sunset.
Day 2 — Deep Ellum mural walk and record shops, live music at night.
Day 3 — Bishop Arts District boutiques and coffee, Dallas World Aquarium before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The DART light rail connects Downtown, Uptown, and Deep Ellum; a rideshare is worth it for Bishop Arts and the Arts District.
guide.stayArea: Uptown or Downtown — walkable to the Arts District and a short DART ride from Deep Ellum.

deals.whyRanked: $159 RT nonstop on Delta or American for October-November travel, with Everglades and Biscayne National Parks both under an hour away.
deals.soloWhy: South Beach's Art Deco streets stay busy and walkable well into the night, though a rental car is what really opens up the two national parks.

highlights: South Beach Art Deco Historic District
Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
Biscayne NP's Dante Fascell Visitor Center
itinerary: Day 1 — South Beach Art Deco walking tour, Lincoln Road, sunset swim.
Day 2 — Everglades NP: Anhinga Trail boardwalk and the Shark Valley bike loop.
Day 3 — Biscayne NP glass-bottom boat tour, then Wynwood Walls before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: A rental car is worth it for the Everglades and Biscayne day trips; South Beach itself is walkable, with the free Freebee shuttle covering Miami Beach.
guide.stayArea: South Beach's Art Deco district — walkable, close to the sand and Lincoln Road.
food: Garcia's Seafood Grille on the Miami River

deals.whyRanked: $228 RT on American (one stop), back on the list after a week away, with Channel Islands National Park a short ferry ride away and a walkable, low-key downtown built for solo trips.

nearbyParks.name: Channel Islands NP (via Ventura Harbor ferry)

deals.soloWhy: A flat, walkable downtown, a free electric shuttle along State Street, and a laid-back beach-town pace make this one of the easiest solo weekends in California.

highlights: State Street shops and tapas bars
Channel Islands NP day trip from Ventura Harbor
itinerary: Day 1 — Stearns Wharf, East Beach boardwalk, sunset at the harbor.
Day 2 — Ferry to Channel Islands NP (Anacapa or Santa Cruz Island) for a half-day hike.
Day 3 — Santa Barbara Mission and Botanic Garden in the morning, State Street tapas crawl before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The free State Street shuttle and MTD buses cover downtown and the waterfront; a rental car (or a short drive to Ventura) is needed for the Channel Islands ferry.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near State Street or the Funk Zone — walkable to the wharf, beach, and shuttle line.

deals.whyRanked: $297 RT nonstop on JetBlue for late-September and October travel, with Mount Rainier and Olympic National Parks both under two and a half hours away.
deals.soloWhy: An extensive bus and light-rail network, a walkable downtown/Capitol Hill core, and a strong cafe culture make solo days easy to fill.

highlights: Capitol Hill cafes and Volunteer Park
itinerary: Day 1 — Pike Place Market, waterfront, Kerry Park at sunset.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Mount Rainier NP: the Skyline Trail loop from Paradise.
Day 3 — Capitol Hill cafes and Volunteer Park in the morning, Museum of Pop Culture before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Link light rail and the bus network cover downtown, Capitol Hill, and the airport; a rental car is required for either national park day trip.
guide.stayArea: Capitol Hill or Downtown — walkable, transit-connected, close to the coffee scene.
